newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Discount Bank offering is still on hold.
newsitem.headline: Discount Bank offering is still on hold.

text.p: Officials involved in the planned offering in Israel Discount Bank said on Sunday they still hoped the offering could go through, despite last-minute objections raised by the Securities Authority.
"I think so, I hope so," said one official when asked whether the Discount prospectus would be published before the end of the month,

The government was due to offer shares and warrants equal to 17 percent of Discount's equity this week, but on Thursday the Securities Authority said it would not approve the prospectus unless it received more exact information on the bank's fourth-quarter doubtful-debt provision.

The bank, Israel's third largest, said earlier that the provision would be significantly higher than previous quarters and would reduce earnings. But Discount said it did not have exact figures on the size of the provision.
A Discount spokeswoman said the bank had no further comment on the offering beyond its announcement last week to the stock exchange.
Meir Jacobson, managing director of MI Holdings, the government company charged with selling the bank shares, denied any agreement had been reached over the weekend.
"There is no agreement....It will take a few more days," said Jacobson.
Discount's prospectus must be published by the end of the month for the offering to be based on third-quarter results.
